messages:
Jordan: heads up — getting a customer escalation (AcmeCorp) for p99 spikes and occasional 401s since the midnight deploy. noticed it lines up with the new continuous-batcher defaults.
Priya: saw the support ticket too. customer reports p99 went from ~700ms -> 2.4s on text.generate endpoints. auth errors intermittent during the same window.
Sam: which config changed in the deploy?
Jordan: deploy changed continuous-batcher default hold_ms from 40 -> 100 and enabled coalesce_grace_window = 8ms for tiny requests. rollout to prod at 00:02 UTC.
Anna: timeline matches. we also rolled a small auth refresh change for bearer token caching at 00:05 but that was just a client-side lib, not server; still, 401s line up. might be two contributing factors.
Jordan: here's the quick perf query I ran (Grafana):
```
p99(latency_ms) by (tenant) where route="/v1/text/generate" and tenant="acme"
// dashboard: https://graf.redwood/services/ingress/dash/tenant-p99?from=now-1h
```
Jordan: CPU and GPU utilization didn't spike, but batch wait time histogram moved right — more requests are sitting in hold window.
Sam: if hold_ms increased, small prompts will wait longer to reach target batch size -> increased tail. the 401s could be auth cache evictions during the wait, client retries hitting a bad path.
Priya: customer shared a sample of their traffic: many tiny requests (~6 tokens) with bursty arrival pattern. seems very sensitive to hold_ms.
Anna: can we reproduce in staging? set their tenant to canary routing and replay traffic?
Jordan: started a replay now against staging cluster with same batching config. reproducing p95->p99 regression locally. attaching log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-14T00:07:12Z] request id=xyz hold_enter ts=1678790832 hold_exit ts=1678790832.112 queued_for=112ms batch_size=3
[2026-03-14T00:07:12Z] auth refresh: token check ok -> downstream 401 on attempt 2
```
Sam: quick mitigation options:
- reduce hold_ms to 20 for tiny-request-tenants
- enable immediate-path for requests < 12 tokens (bypass batching)
- patch auth cache to extend TTL for tokens while queued
We should pick 1-2 and canary.
Anna: prefer config-only change first (no code): reduce global continuous-batcher.hold_ms -> 25 and enable tenant override for acme to 10. roll to 10% canary for 30m.
Priya: tell Acme support we'll try that and we need a short repro window to verify. they can keep traffic at 50% for 15m.
Jordan: applied canary (10%) to acme in us-west-2 with hold_ms=10 at 00:35 UTC. monitoring.
infra-bot: canary rollout started: service=batcher cluster=us-west-2 ring=10% config=continuous-batcher.hold_ms=10 (commit sha: a1b2c3d)
Sam: also pushed short-term auth cache TTL bump on canary path (config only): token_ttl_override=+30s for queued requests.
Jordan: after 5m, p99 down from 2.4s -> 640ms for canary slice, p95 back to normal. 401 rate dropped 85% for that slice.
Priya: Acme replied: "latency much better on your canary, thanks — we still see a few 401s but vastly reduced." :relieved:
Anna: plan: 1) widen canary to 30% for 1h 2) prepare rollback policy if we see any regressions 3) create tenant-specific defaults for tiny-request SaaS customers 4) schedule follow-up to evaluate coalesce_grace_window impact.
Sam: long-term: consider adaptive hold_ms based on prompt length histogram + immediate-path for <N tokens. also need to instrument token TTL vs queue duration more explicitly.
Jordan: I'll draft runbook steps and a follow-up postmortem with repro steps and the exact queries we used.
Priya: please capture customer timeline and the support ticket id in the runbook.
Anna: flagging for eng-oncall to be aware during the wider rollout. I'll coordinate the 30% expand at 02:00 UTC if metrics stay good.
infra-bot: canary expanded to 30% at 00:58 UTC (monitoring window started)
Jordan: final note — this was a config interplay (longer hold + tiny prompts) amplified by token auth TTLs. two mitigations helped: lower hold_ms and short auth-ttl bump while queued. leaving detailed steps in #incidents when we close the ticket.
Priya: thx everyone. updating the ticket and pinging Acme with timeline.
Anna: nice quick pivot :thumbsup:
Sam: follow-up action items: create metric alert for hold_time_histogram shift, add tenant override doc, and propose adaptive hold experiment.
Jordan: added to sprint board (ENG-5129).
Priya: moving to resolved for now pending customer confirmation.
Jordan: closing thread after customer ack.
